source: user-approved business semantics translated into V2 conformance fixtures before comparative execution

s2.principle: available capacity is not committed capacity; a physically feasible binding reservation is not automatically economically acceptable
s2.non_guaranteed_excess_capacity: may be offered but cannot be counted by M as secured future capacity

lender.objective: maximize probability of complete repayment; discretionary decisions evaluate the whole repayment-generating productive system and added exposure
lender.fixture_note: probabilities are prospective conformance inputs, not empirical bank estimates and not outcome-calibrated

transport.principle: accepted service level is a target rather than a physical guarantee; T accepts feasible service when capacity exists and exercises allocation discretion only under capacity conflict

firewall: No V2 comparative A/B/C outcome was inspected or generated in choosing these semantics or fixture values.
